steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Sampling: random (equal chance, unbiased but hard), systematic (every nth, simple but may bias), stratified (proportional, representative but complex), opportunity (available, quick but biased), volunteer (self-selected, motivated but unrepresentative). | Key Fact: Reliability: consistency - repeat study, same results. Improved by: standardised procedures, clear operationalisation. Validity: accuracy - measures what it claims. Improved by: ecological validity, triangulation. | Key Fact: Operationalisation: defining concepts precisely so they can be measured. Example: 'social class' must be operationalised as specific categories. Good operationalisation improves both reliability and validity. | Key Fact: Ethical principles (BSA): informed consent, confidentiality, right to withdra
